question.text: Mr. Vikram Menon, the COO of Tilak Private Credit Fund (Cat II), is comparing the regulatory status of Fund Administrator/Fund Accountant vs Custodian roles. Which statement correctly describes the Indian regulatory position?

answer.text: Both Fund Administrator and Custodian are SEBI-regulated; both need separate registration

Fund Administrator / Fund Accountant is NOT a SEBI-regulated function in India (unlike in several developed markets), whereas Custodian must be registered with SEBI under SEBI (Custodian) Regulations, 1996
Only Fund Administrator is SEBI-regulated; Custodian is self-regulated through APMI
Neither Fund Administrator nor Custodian requires any registration for Cat I/II AIFs

explanation.text: The Logic: The chapter explicitly states 'Fund Accountant or Fund Administrator is not a regulated function in India unlike in other developed markets'. In contrast, all custodians MUST register with SEBI under SEBI (Custodian) Regulations, 1996. The fund administrator function is often bundled by custodians as an add-on service, or performed by third-party vendors or in-house. The Trap: The 'both regulated' option over-regulates fund admin. The inversion option swaps regimes. The 'neither' option under-regulates both (custodian is compulsorily SEBI-registered post-2024 for all AIFs). Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C covers the same contrast. XIX-A (Cat I/II Distributor) may test LP awareness that fund admin is unregulated (hence manager's due-diligence obligation on admin selection). Manager's Pro-Tip: Because fund admin is unregulated, LP diligence packs (esp. FOFs, SWFs) will ask for SSAE-18/SOC-1 reports on your admin's internal controls. Choose an admin that furnishes these reports (Apex, SS&C, Intertrust, Northern Trust, or India-based specialists with SOC-1 coverage).
